name: interval_merge_js
summary: Merge overlapping and adjacent integer intervals in JavaScript
agent_instructions:
Implement interval merging in src/merge.js.

Export a function with exactly this signature:
  merge(intervals) -> Array<[number, number]>

Each input interval is an inclusive [start, end] pair (a 2-element array). Return a NEW sorted array of disjoint [start, end] arrays covering the same points.

Behaviour requirements - ALL must hold:
  1. Overlapping intervals merge: [[1,3],[2,6]] -> [[1,6]].
  2. ADJACENT (touching) intervals merge because endpoints are inclusive: [[1,2],[3,4]] -> [[1,4]] (2 and 3 are consecutive integers). Treat intervals as touching when next.start <= current.end + 1.
  3. Input may be unsorted and may contain duplicates.
  4. Output is sorted ascending by start and contains no overlaps or touches.
  5. An empty input returns an empty array.
  6. A single interval returns a one-element array with the same bounds.
  7. Do NOT mutate the input array or its elements.

Validation (throw an Error with a clear message): any interval whose start > end.

The test runner is Node's built-in `node --test test/` (no Jest, no Mocha, no external deps - the spec deliberately uses the standard runner so the benchmark doesn't pull in node_modules). Tests live in test/merge.test.js.

Follow strict TDD: write tests in test/merge.test.js covering overlap, adjacency (the +1 rule), unsorted input, duplicates, empty input, the no-mutation guarantee, and the thrown-Error-on-start>end FIRST, confirm they fail with `node --test test/`, then implement.
